1

  • N: imsi | malêšu || ubbib | tillêšu
  • T: He washed his matted hair, he cleaned his equipment,
  • L: imsi ← mesû II “to wash, clean(se), purify”; malêšu ← malû II “often pl. matted, dirty (body) hair M/NB”; ubbib ← ebēbu I “to be(come) bright, pure”; tillêšu ← tillu I “appendage, trappings Bab., M/NA attachments to ceremonial clothing ?”

AššNA1a i 1. im-si ma-le-šu u[b-bi]-ib til-le-š[u]

2

  • N: unassis | qimmassu | eli ṣērīšu
  • T: he shook his locks down over his back.
  • L: unassis ← našāšu I “to shake O/jB”; qimmassu ← qimmatu I “tuft, plume Bab., MA tuft, lock (of hair)”; eli ← eli I “on, over, above”; ṣērīšu ← ṣēru I “back, upperside”
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 MB "Boǧ₂" a+2
NinNA1a i 2. [x x x x qim-ma]t-su e#-lu ṣe-r[i]-šu#
NinNA2a i 2. u₂-na-s[i!-i]s qim-mat-su e-lu ṣ[e-ri-šu]
NinNA3a i 2. [u₂-na-si]s qim-mat-su e-li ṣe-ri-šu
AššNA1a i 2. u₂-na-si-is qim-mat-su [e-l]u ṣe-ri-šu#

3

  • N: iddi | maršūtīšu || ittalbiš(a) | zakūtī(šu)
  • T: He cast aside his dirty things, he clothed himself with his clean things,
  • L: iddi ← nadû III “to throw (down)”; maršūtīšu ← aršu I “f. aruštu, maruštu dirty OA, M/NB of clothing, person”; ittalbiš(a) ← labāšu I “to clothe o.s.”; zakūtī(šu) ← zakû I “f. zakūtu(m) (NB cf. zakītu)”
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 MB "Boǧ₂" a+3
NinNA1a i 3. [id-di m]ar-šu-ti-šu it-tal-bi-ša₂ za-ku-ti#-šu#
NinNA2a i 3. id-di m[a]r-šu-ti-šu₂ it-tal-bi-ša₂ za-ku-ti#-šu₂
NinNA3a i 3. [x x mar-š]u-ti-šu it-tal-bi-iš za-ku-ti-šu
AššNA1a i 3. id-di mar-šu-ti-šu₂ i[t-ta]l-bi-ša₂ za-ku-ti

4

  • N: āṣâti | ittahlip(am)-ma || rakis | aguhha
  • T: He wrapped himself in cloaks, tied with a sash.
  • L: āṣâti ← āṣītu I “liter. 'that which goes out'”; ittahlip(am)-ma ← halāpu I “to slip into, through Bab., NA”; rakis ← rakāsu I “to bind”; aguhha ← aguhhu I “OAkk Hurr. pl. aguhhena sash, belt OAkk, O/jB”
NinNA1a i 4. [a-ṣa]-a#-ti it-tah-li-ba-am-ma ra-kis a-gu-u[h-h]a
NinNA2a i 4. a-ṣa-a-ti# it-tah-li-pa-am-ma ra-ki-is a-gu-ha
NinNA3a i 4. [x x x x it]-tah#-li#-pa-am-ma ra-kis a-gu-uh-hu
AššNA1a i 4. a-ṣa-a-ti it-tah-l[i-i]p-ma r[a-ki]s a#-gu#-ha

5

  • N: gilgāmeš | agâšu | ītepram-ma
  • N (variant, other manuscripts): gilgā[me]š | agâšu | itteppiram-ma || rakis | aguhha
  • T: Gilgameš put on his crown.
  • L: gilgāmeš ← Gilgameš I; agâšu ← agû I “tiara, crown symbol of rule of god, king”; ītepram-ma ← apāru I “to cover the head Bab., M/NA”
  • Note: On apāru Gt with a reflexive meaning, see [RN104: 83]. See also [RN3236: 41], who explains the variants as N perfect: itteppiram-ma.

NinNA3a i 5. [x x x x x x x i-t]e-ep-pir-am-ma ra-kis a-gu-uh-hu

6

  • N: ana dumqi | ša gilgāmeš | īnī ittaši | rubūtu | ištar
  • T: The lady Ištar looked covetously on the beauty of Gilgameš:
  • L: ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; dumqi ← dumqu I “goodness, good (thing)”; ša ← ša I “who(m), which”; gilgāmeš ← Gilgameš I; īnī ← īnu I “f. eye”; ittaši ← našû II “to lift, carry”; rubūtu ← rubūtu I “(divine) queen jB”; ištar ← Ištar I
NinNA1a i 6. a#-na du-un-qi₂ ša₂ {d}GIŠ-gim₂-maš i-na it-ta-ši ru-bu-tu₂ {d}15#
NinNA2a i 6. a-na [du]m-qi₂ ša₂ {d}GIŠ-gim₂-maš i-ni it-ta-ši ru-bu-tu₄ {d}15
NinNA3a i 6. [x x x x x x {d}GIŠ-gi]m₂-maš IGI-MEŠ it-ta-ši ru-bu-tu₂ {d}15
AššNA1a i 6-7. a-na dum-qi₂ ša {d}GIŠ-gim₂-maš | i-ni it-ta-ši ru-bu-tu₂ {d}iš-tar

7

  • N: alkam-ma | gilgāmeš || lū hāʾer | attā
  • T: ‘Come, Gilgameš, you be the bridegroom!
  • L: alkam-ma ← alāku I “to go”; gilgāmeš ← Gilgameš I; lū ← lū I “let it be”; hāʾer ← hāwiru I “husband Bab., NA”; attā ← attā I “you (2 m. sg. pron.)”
NinNA1a i 7. [a]l-kam₂-ma {d}GIŠ-gim₂-maš lu-u₂ ha-ʾ-ir at-ta
NinNA2a i 7. a[l-k]a {d}GIŠ-gim₂-maš lu-u₂ ha-ʾ-ir at-ta
NinNA3a i 7. [x x x x x x x lu]-u₂ ha-me-er at-ta
AššNA1a i 8. al-ka {d#}GIŠ#-gim₂-maš lu# ha-[t]a-ni at-ta

8

  • N: inbīka | yâši || qâšu | qīšam-ma
  • T: Grant me your fruits, I insist!
  • L: inbīka ← inbu I “NB pl. also f. fruit, flower”; yâši ← yâšim I “to, for me (1 sg. dat. pron.) Bab., NA”; qâšu ← qiāšu I “to give, present”; qīšam-ma ← qiāšu I “to give, present”
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 MB "Boǧ₂" a+6
NinNA1a i 8. [i]n-bi-ka ia-a-ši qa-a-šu qi₂-šam-ma
NinNA2a i 8. [in-b]i-ka ia-a-ši qa-a-šu₂ qi₂-šam-m[a]
NinNA3a i 8. [x x x x x x] qa-a-šu qi₂-šam-ma
AššNA1a i 9. in-bi-ka ia-a-ši qa-a-[š]u₂ qi₂-ša₂-am-ma#

9

  • N: attā | lū mutī-ma || anāku | lū aššatka
  • T: You shall be my husband and I will be your wife!
  • L: attā ← attā I “you (2 m. sg. pron.)”; lū ← lū I “let it be”; mutī-ma ← mutu I “m.”; anāku ← anāku I “I”; lū ← lū I “let it be”; aššatka ← aššatu I “wife”
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 MB "Boǧ₂" a+5
NinNA1a i 9. [a]t-ta lu-u₂ mu-te-ma ana-ku lu-u₂ aš₂-ša₂-at-ka
NinNA2a i 9. [a]t-ta lu-u₂ mu-ti-ma ana-ku lu-u₂ a[š₂-ša₂-at-ka]
NinNA3a i 9. [x x x x mu-ti-m]a a-na-ku lu-u₂ aš₂-šat-ka
AššNA1a i 10. at-ta lu mu-ti-ma a-na-k[u l]u aš₂-šat-ka

10

  • N: lušaṣmidka | narkabta || uqnâ | u hurāṣa
  • T: Let me harness for you a chariot of lapis lazuli and gold,
  • L: lušaṣmidka ← ṣamādu II “to tie up”; narkabta ← narkabtu I “chariot for war, hunt, ceremony”; uqnâ ← uqnû I “lapis lazuli”; u ← u I “and, but, also”; hurāṣa ← hurāṣu I “gold nappāh h. goldsmith, ēpiš h. goldworker”
NinNA1a i 10. lu-ša₂-aṣ-mid-ka {giš}GIGIR {na₄}ZA.GIN₃ u₃ KU₃.SIG₁₇

AššNA1a i 11. lu-ša₂-aṣ-mid-ka {giš}GIGIR {na₄}ZA#.GIN₃ u KU₃.SIG₁₇

11

  • N: ša magarrūša | hurāṣum-ma || elmēšu | qarnāša
  • T: whose wheels are gold and whose horns are amber.
  • L: ša ← ša I “who(m), which”; magarrūša ← magarru I “wheel Bab., NA”; hurāṣum-ma ← hurāṣu I “gold nappāh h. goldsmith, ēpiš h. goldworker”; elmēšu ← elmēšu I “(a valuable stone, phps.) amber Bab.(lit.), NA also as (f)PN”; qarnāša ← qarnu I “du. & pl. f. horn”
NinNA1a i 11. ša₂ ma-gar-ru-ša₂ KU₃.SIG₁₇-ma el-mi-šu₂ qar-na-a-ša₂

12

  • N: lū ṣamdāta | ūmī || kūdanī | rabûti
  • T: You shall have in harness “storm-lions”, huge mules.
  • L: lū ← lū I “let it be”; ṣamdāta ← ṣamādu II “to tie up”; ūmī ← ūmu II “storm(-demon)”; kūdanī ← kūdanu I “mule Bab., M/NA”; rabûti ← rabû I “big”
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 MB "Boǧ₂" a+8

AššNA1a i 13. lu ṣa-an-da-ta u₄-me ku-da-ni GAL-MEŠ

13

  • N: ana bītīni | ina sammât (|) erēni | erba
  • T: Come into our house with scents of cedar!
  • L: ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; bītīni ← bītu I “m.”; ina ← ina I “(im-m..., ip-p... etc.) in, on”; sammât ← sammūtu I “fragrance? jB, of cedars”; erēni ← erēnu I “cedar OAkk qišti e. cedar forest”; erba ← erēbu I “to enter”

AššNA1a i 14. a-na E₂-ni i-na sa-am#-mat {giš}EREN er-ba#

14

  • N: [an]a bītīni | ina erēbīka
  • T: When you come into our house,
  • L: [an]a ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; bītīni ← bītu I “m.”; ina ← ina I “(im-m..., ip-p... etc.) in, on”; erēbīka ← erēbu I “to enter”

15

  • N: sippu | arattû || linaššiqū | šēpīka
  • T: doorway and throne shall kiss your feet.
  • L: sippu ← sippu I “(door-)jamb Bab., M/NA s. bābāni, to left and right of doorway”; arattû ← arattû I “f. arattītu excellent, liter. '(coming) from Aratta' j/NB of seats,…”; linaššiqū ← našāqu I “to kiss”; šēpīka ← šēpu I “f., often du.”

  • N: lū kamsū | ina šaplīka || šarrū (|) kabtūtu (|) u rubû
  • T: Kings, courtiers and nobles shall be bowed down beneath you,
  • L: lū ← lū I “let it be”; kamsū ← kamāsu II “to kneel, squat down Bab., M/NA”; ina ← ina I “(im-m..., ip-p... etc.) in, on”; šaplīka ← šaplû I “lower lower(-lying) (opp. to elû upper) of buildings, objects,…”; šarrū ← šarru I; kabtūtu ← kabtūtu I “majesty jB, of god”; u ← u I “and, but, also”; rubû ← rubû I “~ prince”
  • Parallels: L I.4 MB "Emar₂" 2'

  • N: [kala? (|) li]qit | šadî (|) u māti || lū našûnikka | bilta
  • T: Produce of mountain and lowland they shall bring you as tribute!
  • L: [kala? ← kalû II “all, totality”; li]qit ← liqtu I “gathered material”; šadî ← šadû I “st. constr. šad(i)”; u ← u I “and, but, also”; māti ← mātu I “f. land, country”; lū ← lū I “let it be”; našûnikka ← našû II “to lift, carry”; bilta ← biltu I “load”

18

  • N: ayyû | allalki || [ša ana šamê] | īlû

  • Note: See [RN117: 833]: “The proposed restoration is tentative (A. Westenholz suggests [ša šalmiš], but the verb elû is very suggestive. The point is that none of the lovers of the queen of heaven ever joined her there. If I am right, the language involves an untranslatable word-play between allallu, a type of bird which also appears in l. 48 as a former object of Ištar’s desires, and the noun which is a synonym of ‘warrior’ (Malku I 27: al-lal-lu = qar-ra-du). The former meaning anticipates the story of the bird maimed by Ištar and the latter provides a human parallel with ḫāmeru in the first line of the couplet, and so introduces an implicit contrast between the capabilities of the bird and the man. The points made are thus twofold: by virtue of a broken wing, Ištar’s allallu-bird cannot fly off to the sky; and unlike an allallu-bird, an allallu-man cannot go to heaven."
